skills.name: Writing health slogans and developing them into paragraphs

note.text:
A slogan is a short, catchy sentence that is easy to remember: “Clean hands, healthy life.” “Sleep under a net, keep malaria away.”
Good slogans are short, use imperatives or rhythm, and give one clear message.
To develop a slogan into a paragraph: the slogan as the first sentence or title; explain why (the reason); give examples or facts; end with an imperative that tells people what to do.

worked_example.problem: Develop the slogan “Clean water, healthy life” into a paragraph.
steps: Why: dirty water carries germs that cause cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea.
How: boil or treat water; keep it covered; wash containers.
End: Drink clean water and protect your family.

cards.idea: A slogan is short, catchy and has one message.
Develop a slogan: reason, examples, closing advice.
example: Dirty water carries germs, so boil it.

cards.idea: End with an imperative telling people what to do.
example: Drink clean water and protect your family.

questions.prompt: Put the sentences of the paragraph in order.

items.text: Dirty water carries germs that cause cholera and typhoid.
Boil or treat your drinking water and keep it covered.
Drink clean water and protect your family.

paper_task.prompt: Write three health slogans in your exercise book. Then choose one and develop it into a paragraph of about 100 words: give the reason, examples, and end with an imperative.
model:
Slogans: “Clean hands, healthy life.” “Sleep under a net, keep malaria away.” “Clean water, healthy life.”

Clean hands, healthy life! Our hands touch many things every day: money, door handles, toilets and food. They carry germs that cause diarrhoea, cholera and coughs. Washing our hands with soap and clean water removes most of these germs. We should wash them before eating, before cooking, after the toilet and after caring for a sick person. It takes less than a minute and costs very little, but it can save a life. Wash your hands often, and teach your little brothers and sisters to do the same.
checklist: My paragraph starts with the slogan.
My sentences are correct and punctuated.
